_comment: Examples under datrix/examples/ that the REAL generation pipeline cannot GENERATE today.
This is a DELIBERATELY MAINTAINED SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an auto-heal: it converts a genuine,
pre-existing generation FAILURE into a loudly-reported skip in the reference-example parity
gate (datrix/scripts/test/reference-example-parity-gate.ps1). It never hides output drift --
a listed (example, language) pair that does generate is still hash-compared against its baseline.
The gate drives the pipeline at ValidationLevel.FAST: every byte-shaping hook runs, the
target-language compile pass (tsc / mvnw compile / dotnet build) does not. A compile failure
of generated output is therefore NEVER a park reason here -- the gate never compiles, and a
pair whose only defect is a build error generates, is blessed, and is hash-compared like any
other. Whether generated output compiles is the generated tier's proof (the generated
project's own tests, run-complete.ps1, generate.ps1 at STANDARD).
KEY FORMAT (language sweep): a bare example_id applies to every registered
language the gate sweeps -- for a failure at config-resolution/deployment-plan-building time,
before any language-specific codegen stage runs (the two entries below). An
'example_id::language' key applies to that one language only -- for a defect in one language's
own codegen stage while the same example generates fine in every other registered language
(a distinction that could not exist before the language sweep made every example genuinely
generatable in every registered language).
All entries reproduce with the sanctioned generator (generate.ps1 <system.dtrx> <out> -L <language>),
so none is a gate artifact. The gate re-attempts every parked, baseline-less pair on every run and
fails loudly the moment one generates, so a stale entry cannot survive the defect it records.
Removing an entry means the defect is FIXED and the example must be blessed.
